author: Amphilochius of Iconium
addressee: The newly baptized and the congregation celebrating their baptism
occasion: A festal homily delivered at Easter, celebrating the newly baptized and the resurrection of Christ.
argument: Amphilochius celebrates the newly baptized as the church's spiritual spring meadow, filled with the fragrance of the Spirit. He urges the congregation to sing the new song, using the Song of Moses at the Red Sea as a type of baptism, in which sin and the devil are drowned. He then expounds the many names of Christ—door, way, sheep, shepherd, pearl, light, cornerstone, sun of righteousness, mustard seed, worm, man—showing how each name reveals a work of Christ for believers. The homily closes by deferring to the teaching of the fathers and blessing the congregation.

outline.move: The homily opens by comparing the newly baptized to a spring meadow and the church to a spiritual garden filled with the fragrance of Christ.
The newly baptized are urged to sing the new song, for baptism has drowned sin and the devil, and believers now wear Christ and will meet the Lord in the air.
The cross is presented as the sail that saves the world from shipwreck, and Christ's many names are introduced and explained one by one.
The remaining names of Christ are explained, and the homily closes by deferring to the fathers' teaching and blessing the congregation.

_unresolved_facts.claim: A festal homily delivered at Easter, celebrating the newly baptized and the resurrection of Christ.
_unresolved_facts.fix: The homily's title mentions 'περὶ τῶν νεοφωτίστων καὶ εἰς τὴν ἀνάστασιν τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ' (concerning the newly baptized and on the resurrection of our Savior Jesus Christ), but the text itself does not explicitly state it was delivered at Easter. The spring imagery and resurrection theme suggest this timing, but the specific liturgical occasion is not directly stated in the body.

_unresolved_facts.claim: He urges the congregation to sing the new song, using the Song of Moses at the Red Sea as a type of baptism, in which sin and the devil are drowned.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Χρησώμεθα παρὰ Μαρίας τῆς ἀδελφῆς Μωϋσέως τὸ ᾆσμα ἐκεῖνο... Συμπαρέστω ἡμῖν καὶ ὁ τῶν ἁγίων ἐκείνων χορὸς καὶ λεγέτω ὃ τότε ἐπὶ τῆς Ἐρυθρᾶς θαλάσσης ἐκελάδιζεν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Amphilochius urges use of Miriam's song, not Moses' song. The source explicitly names 'Μαρίας τῆς ἀδελφῆς Μωϋσέως' (Mary/Miriam the sister of Moses) and 'ὁ τῶν ἁγίων ἐκείνων χορὸς' (the chorus of the saints), referring to the women's chorus led by Miriam, not Moses' song.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The homily closes by deferring to the teaching of the fathers and blessing the congregation.
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἀλλ' ἐπειδὴ ἕκαστος ἡμῶν, ἀγαπητοί, ἐκδέχεται καὶ τὴν τῶν πατέρων μελίρρυτον διδασκαλίαν, ἐνταῦθα τὸ βαλάντιον ἡμῶν τῶν λόγων σφραγισώμεθα
_unresolved_facts.fix: The homily closes by stating that 'each of us awaits the honey-flowing teaching of the fathers' and therefore seals the 'purse of words' here. This is not exactly 'deferring to' the fathers' teaching in the sense of yielding the floor to them, but rather acknowledging that the congregation expects such teaching and so concluding the present discourse.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Miriam... The sister of Moses, whose song at the Red Sea is invoked as a type of baptism
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source calls her 'Μαρίας τῆς ἀδελφῆς Μωϋσέως' (Mary/Miriam the sister of Moses). The brief should note that the Greek form is 'Μαρία' not 'Μιριάμ', and she is explicitly identified as Moses' sister, not separately named as Miriam in the source.

_unresolved_facts.claim: Eve... The first woman, whose fault is healed in Mary
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: οὐκέτι Εὔα φοβεῖται τὸν ὀνειδισμὸν τοῦ Ἀδάμ, ἐν γὰρ Μαρίᾳ τὸ ταύτης πταῖσμα ἀνασέσωσται
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source says Eve's 'πταῖσμα' (stumble/fault) 'ἀνασέσωσται' (has been healed/restored) in Mary. The brief's phrasing 'whose fault is healed in Mary' is acceptable, but should more precisely reflect that Eve's stumble has been restored/healed through Mary.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The psalmist (quoted)... Introduced as 'the psalmist urging us and saying'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: καθὼς ἠκούσαμεν ἀρτίως τοῦ ψαλμῳδοῦ ἡμῖν παραινοῦντος καὶ λέγοντος· Αὕτη ἡ ἡμέρα ἣν ἐποίησεν ὁ κύριος
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source introduces this voice as 'τοῦ ψαλμῳδοῦ' (the psalm-singer/psalmist), not 'the psalmist urging us and saying'—the brief's 'how_marked' should match: 'heard just now the psalm-singer urging us and saying' or similar, reflecting the aorist participle construction.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The holy chorus at the Red Sea (quoted)... Introduced as 'the chorus of the saints' singing at the Red Sea
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Συμπαρέστω ἡμῖν καὶ ὁ τῶν ἁγίων ἐκείνων χορὸς καὶ λεγέτω ὃ τότε ἐπὶ τῆς Ἐρυθρᾶς θαλάσσης ἐκελάδιζεν
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source says 'ὁ τῶν ἁγίων ἐκείνων χορὸς' (that chorus of the saints/holy ones), referring to the Israelites at the Red Sea, not specifically 'the holy chorus at the Red Sea' as a fixed title. The brief should note this is an invited participation, not a direct quotation marker.
